:::caution
This rule is part of the [nursery](/linter/#nursery) group. This means that it is experimental and the behavior can change at any time.
:::
## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.6.3`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/useConsistentLightnessNotation`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule has a [**safe**](/linter/#safe-fixes) fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**information**](/reference/diagnostics#information).
- Sources: 
  - Same as [`lightness-notation`](https://github.com/stylelint/stylelint/blob/main/lib/rules/lightness-notation/README.md)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"useConsistentLightnessNotation": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Enforce a consistent notation for the lightness of colors.

The `lab()`, `lch()`, `oklab()`, and `oklch()` color functions accept their first value,
the lightness, either as a percentage or as a number. Both notations describe the same
color: `oklch(85% 0.17 88)` and `oklch(0.85 0.17 88)` are equal. Writing lightness the same
way everywhere makes colors easier to read and compare.

For `oklab()` and `oklch()`, the number `1` equals `100%`. For `lab()` and `lch()`, the
number `100` equals `100%`.

## Examples

### Invalid

```css
a { color: oklch(0.85 0.17 88); }
```

### Valid

```css
a { color: oklch(85% 0.17 88); }
a { color: oklab(86% -0.2 0.15); }
a { color: lch(85% 60 88); }
a { color: lab(86% -40 30); }
a { color: oklch(from red 50% c h); }
```

## Options

### `notation`

Default: `"percentage"`

Whether lightness is written as a percentage (`"percentage"`) or as a number (`"number"`).

```json title='biome.json'
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"useConsistentLightnessNotation": {
					"level": "on",
					"options": {
						"notation": "number"
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

```
